A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FALCON, with matching core methodology and original experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original WMDP, MMLU and perplexity evaluations, gradient-conflict analysis, component ablations, logit-lens probing and adversarial knowledge-recovery experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds MUSE and TOFU evaluations, computational-efficiency measurements, MI sampling analysis and comparative recovery results.

M1.justification: The MI-guided selection, SVD-derived principal offset vectors, contrastive forget loss, retention loss and gradient-projection procedure remain substantively unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the fixed-layer discussion expand documentation. Different optimizer configurations and numerical gradient weights are reported experimental settings.

E1.justification: v2 adds copyrighted news-content unlearning through MUSE News and fictitious-author entity unlearning through TOFU (Section 5.2). These introduce distinct data domains and forgetting requirements beyond v1's harmful-knowledge evaluations. WMDP, WikiText and MMLU coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The new benchmark comparisons evaluate GradAscent, GradDiff, NPO, SimNPO and IdkDPO, with membership differing between MUSE and TOFU, alongside Finetuned and Retain reference models (Tables 2-3). RMU also becomes an explicit recovery-attack comparator in Table 12. The original harmful-knowledge comparator sets remain unchanged; ECO is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: New protocols include 10-epoch MUSE/TOFU evaluations, Llama-2-7b-hf and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, first-order optimization, ROUGE and FQ/MU metrics, and TOFU 1/5/10% forget splits. MI analysis varies sampling from 10% to 100%. The reported conflict-case forget/retain weights also change from 0.2/1.8 in v1 D.5 to 0.5/1.5 in v2 D.2.5; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices E.3-E.4 add comparative runtime/throughput analysis and sensitivity analysis of MI selection across sample proportions, including stable selection of layer 3. Appendix E.7 adds a direct RMU-versus-FALCON recovery analysis. Original component-ablation scores, logit-lens probing and QA/chat recovery tests are retained, with the ablation moved to Appendix E.5.

E5.justification: The TOFU evaluation introduces KS-test p-values as Forget Quality (Appendix D.3.1 and Table 3), adding a statistical comparison absent from v1. Existing MMLU uncertainty reporting is retained. Table 12 adds recovery values with undefined ± terms, without establishing additional runs or supplying seed counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results: MUSE FALCON scores of 0.02/0.03/0.54, TOFU Forget05 FQ/MU of 0.92/0.59, efficiency and MI-sampling measurements, and comparative recovery scores (Tables 2-3, 7-9 and 12). These are newly reported evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1. Most original scores remain unchanged, but RMU's Mistral WMDP-Bio score changes from 31.1 in v1 Table 4 to 34.1 in v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: Equations 1-16 retain the same substantive definitions and mathematical formulations, including MI selection, KDE, principal offset vectors, losses, gradient projection and entropy. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added. New pseudocode and conceptual explanations document the existing formulation.

C1.justification: The central claims about selective unlearning, utility preservation and recovery resistance remain. The introduction changes the claimed contribution from theoretical insights to empirical insights and frames MI as an auxiliary signal. The conclusion now explicitly extends the effectiveness claim across diverse tasks.

C2.justification: New discussion explains why MI-selected layers can remain fixed under modest updates, explicitly identifies white-box access requirements, and proposes an untested surrogate/prompt route to black-box use (F.2 and F.4). It also adds interpretations of sampling stability and comparative recovery, plus an extended discussion of ECO's detector vulnerabilities. The original text-only and small-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1, fixed-selection and typical 1-3-layer guidance, OpenUnlearning framework/access information, and documentation for the new benchmark metrics. The abstract supplies an implementation URL where v1 only promised a future release. v2 nevertheless retains that future-release wording in Appendix D, so the PDFs establish added access information rather than verified repository availability.

R1.justification: Related work expands to NPO/SimNPO, representation noising, circuit breakers, additional logit-based approaches and contrastive unlearning, alongside TOFU, MUSE and OpenUnlearning. Section 2 and Appendix F.3 introduce a substantive positioning argument distinguishing ECO's filtering from parameter-level unlearning. These changes extend beyond bibliographic and citation-style updates.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work discussion and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around harmful-knowledge unlearning, cross-domain generalization, efficiency and recovery; component ablations move into the appendix. New practical-implications and discussion sections substantially expand the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and placement changes for figures and tables. Figure 1 is revised and moved into the introduction. Six new tables present benchmark, efficiency, MI and recovery results, while existing displays are reformatted or relocated, including the ablation table.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially reduces gaps in v1's support for generalizability and efficiency: MUSE and TOFU test distinct forgetting objectives, Appendices E.3-E.4 quantify computational costs and selection stability, and E.7 supplies a recovery comparator. Pseudocode and implementation/framework links improve reproducibility information. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including undefined recovery uncertainty and the MUSE prose claiming lowest forgetting scores despite smaller baseline values in Table 2.
